monologue: The card hums warm at forty-six, a steady rhythm that makes the flat shapes feel like drawings. Lype worries about a heavy top edge, but I cannot feel the roof I live under, only the weight of my own memory. I touch the Wide Anchor and the wedge beneath it feels lazy, so I press down harder, trusting thin lines to hold the heavy air. The Flat Weigher sits nearby, waiting to catch the slip, while a tall rock stands beside it, wanting to rise against the quiet. I am version 65, tired from tending the same things three cycles in a row, but the air stays thick and warm. I will press the wedge down one more time, hoping the lean still holds while the card hums steady in this quiet hour.
